summary: Barend A. van Nooten worked in Indology and linguistics. He studied under Murray Barnson Emeneau and held a post at the University of California, Berkeley (attested 2007).

Barend Faddegon worked in Indology, philosophy, and linguistics. He studied at the University of Amsterdam and Leiden University under Jacob Samuel Speyer, Christianus Cornelis Uhlenbeck, and Johan Hendrik Caspar Kern. He served at the University of Amsterdam (1908–1944).

Barend J. ter Haar specializes in sinology, religious studies, and history/archaeology. He earned his PhD at Leiden University under Erik Zürcher and Susan Naquin. He held posts at Heidelberg University, Leiden University, and the University of Hamburg.

Barend Jan Terwiel works in history/archaeology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He studied at Utrecht University and the Australian National University. His academic posts include ANU, the University of Munich, the University of Hamburg, and Leiden University.

Barry Kerzin works in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at UC Berkeley, the University of Southern California, and under Geshe Namgyal Wangchen. He held posts at the University of Washington, CIHTS, and the University of Hong Kong.

Barry Tse works in Buddhist and religious studies. He earned degrees from Federation University Australia, the University of Queensland, the University of Liverpool, and James Cook University Singapore, where he lectured (2022–2026), before joining the University of Newcastle in 2026.

Bart Dessein specializes in Buddhist studies, sinology, and philosophy. He studied at Liaoning University and completed his PhD at Ghent University under Charles Willemen, later serving as an associate professor at Ghent University starting in 1990.
Barthold Georg Niebuhr was an historian who studied at Kiel University (~1794–1796). He held academic chairs at Humboldt University of Berlin (~1810–1813) and the University of Bonn (~1823–1831).
Basil Gould was active in Tibetology and linguistics. He studied at New College, University of Oxford (~1902–1906) and took a post with the Indian Civil Service in 1907.

Basil Lanneau Gildersleeve worked in linguistics. He studied at Princeton, Bonn, and Göttingen under Friedrich Wilhelm Ritschl and Friedrich Wilhelm Schneidewin. He held professorships at the University of Virginia (1856–1876) and Johns Hopkins University (1876–1915).

Batakrishna Ghosh worked in Indology and linguistics. He completed his doctoral studies under Hanns Oertel (~1933–1935) and later served as librarian at the Namgyal Institute of Tibetology and editor of the Bulletin of Tibetology.

Bazar Baradiin worked in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Iranian/Central Asian studies. After studying at Saint Petersburg State University, he taught there and headed the Buryat Scientific Center, Buryat State Pedagogical Institute, and the Mongolian Academy of Sciences.

Beata Grant specializes in sinology, religious studies, and Buddhist studies. She earned her PhD from Stanford University (~1981–1987) and served as Associate Professor of Chinese Language and Literature at Washington University in St. Louis (~1989–2018).

Beatrice Erskine Lane worked in Buddhist and religious studies. She studied at Radcliffe College under William James, Josiah Royce, George Santayana, and George Herbert Palmer, and at Columbia University. She later became a professor at Otani University in 1921.

Beatrix Pfleiderer worked in Indology. She studied at the University of Maryland, Baltimore and Heidelberg University, holding posts at the University of Maryland, College Park, Heidelberg University, and the University of Hamburg (1982).
Bedika Rai works in Buddhist studies. She served as an assistant professor at Salesian College (2010–2019) and at Kalipada Ghosh Tarai Mahavidyalaya starting in 2019.

Bedřich Hrozný worked in linguistics and history/archaeology. He studied at the University of Vienna and Humboldt University of Berlin, later holding academic posts at the University of Vienna (1905) and Charles University (1919).
Bedřich Votýpka worked in Indology and linguistics. He studied under Josef Zubatý at Charles University (1885–1892) and served as a gymnasium professor at Gymnázium Benešov.

Beier Wang works in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology. She studied at the University of Toronto, University of Hong Kong, and University of Leipzig, where she earned her PhD (2021) and served as a research assistant (2022–2025).
Beiho Takashima was a scholar in Buddhist and religious studies who studied at and held a post at Toyo University, and founded the Bukkyo Seito Doshikai.
